_comment: Findings the profile lint job tolerates. class: not-applicable (rule does not apply to a private PKI, or a deliberate choice), known-gap (optional improvement), known-defect (real defect, not yet fixed). Every entry needs a reason; unused entries are reported as stale.

entries.reason: Requires a CABF certificatePolicies reserved OID. CA/B Forum rule for publicly trusted TLS; Kryptkeeper issues private-PKI certificates that carry no CABF policy OID.

BR 7.1.2.7.9 deprecates subject CN for public TLS. The hub keeps CN for private clients that still key on it; RFC 5280 permits it.
Same as w_subject_common_name_included: public-TLS DV rule, RFC 5280 permits CN.
BR discourages a leaf SKI to save bytes. RFC 5280 recommends it and chain building in private hierarchies uses it.
Same as w_ext_subject_key_identifier_not_recommended_subscriber.
RSA serverAuth leaves keep keyEncipherment on purpose: TLS 1.2 RSA key-exchange peers require it. Not a standards violation; the BR only discourages it.
Short-lived (<=7 day) leaves deliberately omit CRL/OCSP pointers (internal/ca shortLivedMax), modelled on the BR short-lived exemption.
Same as e_sub_cert_aia_missing: short-lived certificates intentionally carry no revocation pointers.

Same as e_sub_cert_aia_missing: short-lived certificates intentionally carry no revocation pointers.
Roots set pathLenConstraint=1 deliberately to bound hierarchy depth; the BR advice to omit it is for public roots.
Requires a CABF certificatePolicies reserved OID. CA/B Forum rule for publicly trusted TLS; Kryptkeeper issues private-PKI certificates that carry no CABF policy OID.
Requires a CABF certificatePolicies reserved OID. CA/B Forum rule for publicly trusted TLS; Kryptkeeper issues private-PKI certificates that carry no CABF policy OID.
CABF TLS BR 7.1.2.8.2 only; RFC 6960 does not forbid a CRL pointer on a delegated responder certificate.
Public S/MIME BR rules (validated-name sources, reserved policy OIDs). CA/B Forum rule for publicly trusted TLS; Kryptkeeper issues private-PKI certificates that carry no CABF policy OID.

Hub-issued intermediates carry no cRLDistributionPoints or AIA. Optional in RFC 5280 for a private hierarchy, but relying parties cannot revocation-check or fetch the issuer from the CA certificate. Improvement, not a defect.

Hub-issued intermediates carry no cRLDistributionPoints or AIA. Optional in RFC 5280 for a private hierarchy, but relying parties cannot revocation-check or fetch the issuer from the CA certificate. Improvement, not a defect.
The hub never publishes a caIssuers URL for its CA certificates, so leaves carry only OCSP. Optional per RFC 5280; chains are delivered out of band. Improvement.
Same as w_sub_cert_aia_does_not_contain_issuing_ca_url.
Same: no caIssuers URL is published.

The engine ignores CSR emailAddresses (leafIssuanceParams has no email field), so an emailProtection template yields a certificate with no rfc822Name SAN and no way to name the mailbox. S/MIME is not really supported; fixing it needs a name-policy design (who may claim which mailbox), not a drive-by change.
